entries.title: Sky sign Morgan Maly to development contract
entries.summary: <p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/chicago-sky" target="_blank" >Sky</a> signed Morgan Maly, a former Creighton standout, to a development contract. She will be available for the Sky’s next game Friday at home against the Valkyries.</p><p>The Sky had two development spots open after forward <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/chicago-sky/2026/08/18/mercury-poach-forward-maddy-westbeld-from-sky" >Maddy Westbeld</a> signed a rest-of-season contract with the Mercury. Even with only eight games remaining, there is value in adding a development player now because the Sky can retain her rights for next season.</p><p>Maly, a 6-1 shooter, went undrafted out of Creighton and signed a training camp contract with the Sun. She then played overseas in Greece, where she averaged 18.7 points and 9.7 rebounds while shooting 36.6% from three-point range on 6.6 attempts per game.</p><p>Maly spent 2026 training camp with the Mercury but did not make the team.</p><p>The Sky are on the cusp of being eliminated from playoff contention, sitting six games out of the eighth and final playoff spot.</p><bsp-list-loadmore entries.title: White Sox hold Cubs to two hits, avoid sweep with shutout win in Crosstown series finale
entries.summary: <p>No bats? No brooms.</p><p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" >Cubs</a> learned that the hard way Wednesday, with <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox" >White Sox</a> pitching silencing the second highest scoring offense in baseball in a 3-0 win that prevented a Crosstown sweep at Wrigley Field.</p><p>Led by six nearly perfect innings of relief from righty Jose Urquidy, Sox pitchers kept the Cubs to just two hits.</p><p>The Sox got the game’s first run in the sixth inning, finally breaking through against Cubs starter Clay Holmes with back-to-back hits from Miguel Vargas and Andrew Benintendi.</p><p>They struck again in the eighth, when outfielder Braden Montgomery doubled off Michael Busch’s glove at first base, bringing home a pair and creating some late-inning breathing room.</p><p>The Cubs mustered only a single scoring chance, and that was immediately erased. Outfielder Tyrone Taylor, who had both hits, doubled to start the Cubs’ half of the sixth inning, but he belatedly tagged on a Pete Crow-Armstrong lineout to right field, with Montgomery throwing him out at third base by a wide margin.</p><p>Urquidy, acquired in a July trade, was excellent, retiring 17 of the 19 hitters he faced and striking out eight.</p><p>The Cubs played their typical brand of terrific defense, with third baseman Alex Bregman, in particular, shining in the field a day after <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/18/cubs-white-sox-crosstown-alex-bregman-pete-crow-armstrong-munetaka-murakami-kevin-gausman" >he drove in the tying and winning runs Tuesday night</a>. But good pitching and good defense wasn’t enough on a quiet day for the bats.</p><p>The Sox salvaging a victory Wednesday gave them a seventh win in their last 11 games.</p><p></p><p></p><bsp-listcarousel class="PageListE" data-module data-column-count=3 data-hide-authors="true" data-hide-categories="true" data-hide-dates="true" data-hide-descriptions="true" data-show-loadmore="true" ><a class="AnchorLink" id="list-c90005" name="list-c90005"></a><div class="PageList-header" > <div class="PageList-header-title-wrap" > <div class="PageList-header-title"> <a class="" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" target="{borderColor=#dfdfdf, pageNumber=1, titleUrl=https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs, inverseColors=false, footerBgColor=#000000, title=Latest on the Cubs, bodyFont=font-3, showListNumbers=false, imagePositionHorizontal=null, rteBodyFont=font-3, headerBottomBorderColor=#111010, subTitle=null, stickyHeader=true, pageCount=4731, listTitleColor=#000000, tableCellBorderColor=#ccd1d5, relatedListFont=font-1, hideAuthors=true, tertiaryTextColor=#6c6c6c, buttonHoverTextColor=#ffffff, tableFont=font-1, carouselAutoPlay=false, promoTitleFont=font-2, ctaButtonText=[], items=[{title=Acusan a hombre de darle puñetazo a otro aficionado en el partido de los Cubs contra los Sox en Wrigley Field, type=Image, wordCount=231, _styledTemplate=null, imageAlignment=null, isFeatured=false, description=[{items=[La pelea no estaba relacionada con una riña en las gradas captada en un video ampliamente compartido en redes sociales, según la Policía de Chicago. entries.title: Anthony Kay is leaning on soft stuff to provide a firm presence in White Sox rotation
entries.summary: <p>After posting a Yokohama franchise-record 1.55 ERA last season, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox" >White Sox</a> starter <b>Anthony Kay</b> had comparable offers to stay in Japan, but the 31-year-old signed a two-year, $12 million pact with the White Sox to prove himself as a big league starter.</p><p>In compiling a 6.12 ERA through April, Kay got a demonstration of what major leaguers can do, even against 96 mph from the left side.</p><p>“In Japan, you can kind of overpower guys there because they don't see velocity as much,” Kay told the Sun-Times. “I had to change my repertoire a little bit over here, rely on the soft stuff a little bit more because guys can handle velo.”</p><p>Specifically, Kay needed to show he could locate soft stuff in the strike zone, not just as chase pitches. Like many pitchers after Tommy John surgery, the action on Kay’s changeup is different from when it was his best pitch in college. He credits changing where the catcher sets up for helping him visualize where he wanted his changeup and sweeper to land; low and away from right-handed hitters.</p><p>“[Hitters] have to respect that,” said pitching coach <b>Zach Bove</b>. “If he's landing the changeup and the sweeper, it slows them down to make the four-seam and the cutter play up even more.”</p><p>With that dynamic in place, Kay is now a stabilizing force in a Sox rotation where he once resembled a weak link, and is running a 3.46 ERA since May 1.</p><h3><b>White Sox rotation is in place, if you squint</b></h3><p>Manager <b>Will Venable</b> stipulated Wednesday that <b>Erick Fedde </b>and <b>Jose Urquidy </b>are part of the Sox rotation at present, though both pitched behind openers in the Crosstown series, and the former has bounced between roles throughout August.</p><p>“Technically on paper, it’s not the five starters,” Venable said. “But you look at Fedde and the way we have used him as a guy in the rotation spot, that is his spot. You saw what happened [Tuesday]. That was no different than how we have used him before. The only difference is we used him recently out of the pen as well. You expect that’s a spot he can cover, and then in the case of Urquidy, same type of deal.”</p><p>Fedde was moved to the bullpen when the Sox traded for <b>Luis Castillo</b>, back when their rotation included a healthy <b>Davis Martin</b> and <b>Noah Schultz,</b> before the latter was optioned. With 4⅔ innings of scoreless baseball Tuesday, Fedde should be in the starter mix for at least another turn.</p><h3><b>Injury updates</b></h3><h3></h3><p>Martin threw his first bullpen session Wednesday since hitting the IL for a blister on his right middle finger. The blister is basically healed, but the IL stay also offers Martin the chance to rest and reset his delivery mechanics. After a phenomenal first two months, he has a 7.06 ERA since June 1. He is eligible to be activated on Aug. 29.</p><p><b>Kyle Teel</b> is on track to test his recovering left ankle running the bases this weekend. If he completes two successful days of running the bases, the Sox starting catcher will be cleared for a rehab assignment with Triple-A Charlotte.</p><p>Prospect lefty <b>Cameron Johnson</b> underwent surgery to remove loose bodies from his pitching elbow this week. Last month’s 15th round pick is expected to be ready by spring.</p><p></p><div class="PageListL" data-module data-hide-authors="true" data-hide-categories="true" data-hide-dates="true" entries.title: Jesse White Tumbling Team impresses judges with live show performance on ‘America’s Got Talent’
entries.summary: <p>Chicago’s Jesse White Tumbling Team exhibited their time-tested winning form Tuesday night <a class="Link" href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6OMWRQEDz1Q" target="_blank" >during their quarterfinals set on “America’s Got Talent.”</a></p><p>Performing to the pulsating rhythms of Jamiroquai’s “Canned Heat,” the tumblers continued their quest for a $1 million prize on the hit reality competition series, once again wowing the judges and the audience inside the Pasadena Civic Auditorium.</p><p>Utilizing two across-stage runs of gymnastic mats, the team flew in and out at a frenetic pace — rolling, jumping, somersaulting and flying through the air, at one point even towering up and over the organization’s 92-year-old founder, Jesse White.</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/movies-and-tv/2026/08/17/jesse-white-tumbling-team-americas-got-talent" target="_blank" >Jesse White Tumbling Team gets second chance on ‘America’s Got Talent’ as troupe rolls into live rounds </a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" data-embed> <iframe width="200" height="113" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/6OMWRQEDz1Q?feature=oembed" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen title="Jesse White Tumbling Team Brings the HEAT With 92-Year-Old Jesse White | Quarterfinals | AGT 2026"></iframe> </div> </div></div><p>Judge Simon Cowell praised the performance, commenting: “Well, I loved your first audition, and then I was thinking, Can they make it better on the live shows? Can I be honest? It was better.”</p><p>The team is hoping “better” translated into votes, as their continuing on in the show depends on viewer voting, which ended at 6 a.m. Wednesday.</p><p>“I hope the people at home vote,” judge Howie Mandel said. Turning his comments to the audience in the building, he added, “You gotta vote.”</p><p>Eleven teams competed in this first quarterfinals heat, with South Korean magic act Hundred Fingers earning the coveted “golden buzzer” from Mandel, automatically propelling them past the semifinal rounds and into the finals in September.</p><p>The rest of the acts will know if they move on to the semifinals — or not — when the voting results are televised on Wednesday night during the results show, airing at 7 p.m. on NBC. Only the three out of the 10 remaining acts advance to the next round based on total audience votes.</p><p><i>Miriam Di Nunzio is the former Features Editor of the Chicago Sun-Times.</i><br></p>

entries.title: Suburban man caught with Molotov cocktails taken into ICE custody, faces federal charges
entries.summary: <p>A suburban man arrested after a police search found Molotov cocktails in his backpack was released on electronic monitoring — but taken into custody by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents two days later.</p><p>Hamed Alsaidi, 31, was arrested Aug. 1 after Mokena police officers searched him and found eight glass bottles filled with an ignitable liquid, with cloth stuffed into the bottle openings, according to Mokena Police Chief Brian Benton.</p><p>Inside the backpack was a map of Orland Park and the word “mosque” written on it.</p><p>Officers initially found Alsaidi lurking at a gas station at 187th Street and Wolf Road, Benton said. Officers gave him a ride to a nearby convenience store. A few hours later, officers once again spotted Alsaidi walking in the middle of 191st Street near LaGrange Road. Alsaidi gave officers a false name and was taken into custody and searched. He was charged with unlawful use of a weapon and obstructing a peace officer.</p><p>Alsaidi, of Oak Forest, appeared at a detention hearing Aug. 2, when Will County Judge Theodore Jarz granted his pretrial release with electronic monitoring under the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/columnists/2026/01/09/pritzker-illinois-house-speaker-welch-open-tweaking-safe-t-act-electronic-monitoring-rich-miller" target="_blank" ><u>SAFE-T Act</u></a>, after determining that conditions could mitigate the risks of his release.</p><p>He was taken into ICE custody two days later, according to the Department of Homeland Security. Officials said Alsaidi, an immigrant from Jordan, illegally entered the U.S. through California in March 2024.</p><p>Federal officials said ICE lodged a detainer with Will County on the day Alsaidi was arrested by Mokena police. But instead of honoring the detainer, county officials released him Aug. 2 without notifying ICE.</p><p>Alsaidi was charged Monday in federal court with felony unlawful possession of a weapon and obstructing identification, according to federal prosecutors.<br></p>

entries.title: Bears training camp report No. 16: QB Tyson Bagent remains out
entries.summary: <p>Breaking down the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" >Bears’</a> Wednesday training camp practice:<br> </p><h3><b>What happened</b></h3><p>Second-string quarterback Tyson Bagent remained sidelined by a hamstring injury when the Bears held an hourlong practice on the backfields of Halas Hall. Case Keenum, who had a perfect 158.3 passer rating against the Browns, practiced with the second team. He figures to play more snaps Saturday than any other quarterback.</p><p>Defensive tackle Grady Jarrett and left guard Joe Thuney each received a veteran’s day off to prepare to Thursday’s joint practice in Cincinnati. </p><p>Practice ended as players cheered their coaches participating in an end zone drill.</p><h3><b>Davenport ‘disruptive’</b></h3><h3></h3><p>Defensive end Marcus Davenport has yet to practice since he signed with the Bears earlier this week, but defensive coordinator Dennis Allen thinks he’ll be able to help his pass rush soon enough.</p><p>Allen was part of the Saints team that drafted Davenport in Round 1 in 2018.</p><p>“He's always been a disruptive player,” Allen said.</p><p>The issue in recent years has been his health. He played 15 games in 2022 and 14 total since.</p><p>“The biggest thing for Marcus, and it's been that way throughout his career, it’s his ability to be healthy and maintain his health,” Allen said. “But when he's out there, he's a disruptive force.”</p><h3><b>What’s next</b></h3><p>The Bears hustled out of Halas Hall after practice to fly to Cincinnati, putting the 260 or so members of their traveling party through security screening on-site.They’ll practice against the Bengals from 9-11 a.m. Thursday at Kettering Health Practice Fields adjacent to Paycor Stadium.</p><bsp-list-loadmore entries.title: Woman, 64, and man, 25, gunned down in West Garfield Park double homicide
entries.summary: <p>Police are looking for two assailants who opened fire, fatally shooting a 25-year-old man and killing a 64-year-old woman a block away at midday on the city's West Side. </p><p>At 11:55 a.m. the 25-year-old was standing outside in the 200 block of South Pulaski Road when two unknown gunmen approached and at least one of them opened fire, shooting the 25-year-old, according to Chicago police.</p><p>At the same time, a 64-year-old woman was found dead in the 300 block of South Pulaski Road with a gunshot wound to the chest, police said. </p><p>Both were taken to Mount Sinai Hospital, where they were pronounced dead, according to police. </p><p>The gunmen sped away in a black car, southbound on Pulaski Road. </p><p>No other injuries were reported. </p><p>Area 4 detectives are investigating.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-7c0000" name="image-7c0000"></a> entries.title: Gary residents still in the dark as power outage could drag for 2 weeks after last week's deadly storms
entries.summary: <p>Thousands of Gary residents could go two weeks without power after last week's deadly storms caused outages across Indiana. </p><p>The state's utility company NIPSCO reported that over 60% of its customers — roughly 370,000 homes — lost power during the Aug. 11 storm and subsequent days of severe weather.</p><p>And while many customers across the state have their lights back on, about 22,000 customers in Gary were still without power, local and state officials told reporters Wednesday afternoon. </p><p>Power likely won't be completely restored to the city until 11:59 p.m. on Tuesday — two weeks after the Aug. 11 storm, said Melody Birmingham, the group utilities president at NiSource, NIPSCO's parent company. </p><p>Gary also has the largest number of customers in the state waiting for power to return, Birmingham said during Wednesday's press conference. Part of why it's taking longer to restore power is the city suffered the most "extensive and complex damage" from the storm, mainly because of the 99 mph winds that tore through Northwest Indiana and knocked down several large trees, she said. </p><p>"Those winds were as strong as a Category 2 hurricane," Birmingham said. </p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div "Progress is being made, power is actively being turned on. But many residents are still suffering without power."</p><p>Birmingham said crews of linemen were not only repairing downed power lines, in some places they're rebuilding electrical systems that were destroyed in some places. </p><p>That includes 335 damaged poles that need to be repaired or replaced and 27 outages at substations that need to be fixed before power can be restored, she said. </p> <p>Birmingham acknowledged that residents need better communication and updates from NIPSCO. That caused a lot of confusion and anger for residents, Melton said.</p><p><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/weather/2026/08/17/gary-indiana-residents-without-power-deadly-storms" target="_blank" >Residents also told the Sun-Times</a> on Monday that they hadn't heard any updates from NIPSCO on when their power would be back. </p><p>But Birmingham pushed back on the criticism that Gary is low on NIPSCO's priority list. </p><p>"This is not about a socioeconomic divide, this is truly because of the area the storm hit," she said. "We have not and should not ever prioritize who we serve based on color, based on socioeconomic status. That is not the business we are in."</p>

entries.title: Cook County Board of Review urges residents to start on appeals for 2026 tax bills after recent storm damage
entries.summary: <p>The Cook County Board of Review has opened pre-filling appeals for next year's property taxes, allowing homeowners whose property was damaged in recent storms to start the process of reducing their 2027 tax bill.</p><p>The second installment of 2025 property tax bills are expected to hit mailboxes on or before Sept. 1, according to the board. </p><p>The deadline for filing exemptions for the first installment of 2026 tax bills closes the first day of September as well, and Board chair George Cardenas urged people to check their exemptions. </p><p>He explained sometimes seniors will fall off the senior freeze list, and property owners who recently made a purchase may also have to file for new exemptions.</p><p>The first group of townships eligible to file an appeal — Evanston, New Trier, Norwood Park, Oak Park, River Forest, Riverside and Rogers Park townships — also have until Sept. 1 to file an appeal for next year's first installment, and until Sept. 11 to submit evidence for claims.</p><p>While storm damage relief isn’t available for the tax bills property owners in the county just received, the damage from this year could be reflected on 2027 charges if the proper forms and evidence are submitted, board officials said.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a entries.title: Promotor de Ford City Mall modifica los planes del proyecto antes de la primera audiencia municipal
entries.summary: <p>El promotor inmobiliario que quiere transformar el cerrado Ford City Mall en un campus industrial podría recibir sus primeras aprobaciones municipales esta semana, tras ampliar sus planes para incluir una plaza pública y una nueva estación de autobuses de la Autoridad de Tránsito de Chicago (CTA).</p><p>Kurv Industrial, con sede en Chicago y antes conocida como Bridge Industrial, planea demoler Ford City Mall y construir un <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz/2025/07/17/ford-city-mall-ha-ido-perdiendo-su-atractivo-y-podria-ser-convertido-en-bodegas" target="_blank" >campus industrial</a> de cuatro edificios. El proyecto será considerado por la Comisión de Planificación de Chicago el jueves.</p><p>Los planes de Kurv presentados ante la Comisión muestran una nueva plaza patrimonial de Ford City que celebra "más de 80 años de historia de Chicago", con áreas ajardinadas y asientos. También incluye una nueva estación de autobuses de la CTA a lo largo de la avenida Kostner, al este del centro comercial.</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-a60000" name="module-a60000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h3>La Voz Chicago WhatsApp</h3>Encuentra más noticias en nuestro canal de WhatsApp. <a class="Link" href="https://www.whatsapp.com/channel/0029Vb0XT1XCHDylm3rCs40P" target="_blank" ><b>Síguenos.</b></a></div> </div><p>La plaza y la estación de autobuses podrían hacer que los planes de Kurv sean más atractivos para los comisionados. Los almacenes y proyectos industriales a menudo enfrentan una fuerte oposición comunitaria por su falta de usos y espacios públicos, además de preocupaciones por el <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/the-watchdogs/2026/05/12/warehouse-boom-next-day-delivery-die-80-amazon-centerpoint-intermodal-northpoint-joliet-manhattan-elwood" target="_blank" >aumento del tráfico, el ruido y la contaminación del aire</a>.</p><p>El concejal Derrick Curtis (18.º), cuyo distrito incluye el centro comercial, dijo en una carta a sus constituyentes, publicada en su sitio web, que el cierre del centro comercial representa "el fin de un capítulo importante", pero que también debe marcar el comienzo de algo nuevo y mejor.</p><p>"Mi prioridad es asegurar que esta propiedad no quede abandonada", escribió Curtis. "Debemos procurar una reurbanización responsable que proteja nuestros vecindarios, cree oportunidades económicas, fortalezca nuestra base de impuestos y traiga nuevas inversiones productivas al distrito 18".</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-d46c60" name="image-d46c60"></a> <picture data-crop="medium"> <source type="image/webp" width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/9f9956a/2147483647/strip/true/crop/3000x1684+0+187/resize/490x275!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Feb%2F8f%2F296777b64562a5d4c90ef513ef83%2Ffordcity-07xx25-4.jpg 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/133af63/2147483647/strip/true/crop/3000x1684+0+187/resize/980x550!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Feb%2F8f%2F296777b64562a5d4c90ef513ef83%2Ffordcity-07xx25-4.jpg 2x" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <source width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/8241b29/2147483647/strip/true/crop/3000x1684+0+187/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Feb%2F8f%2F296777b64562a5d4c90ef513ef83%2Ffordcity-07xx25-4.jpg" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <img class="Image" alt="Vista aérea del centro comercial Ford City en 7601 S. Cicero Ave." srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/8241b29/2147483647/strip/true/crop/3000x1684+0+187/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Feb%2F8f%2F296777b64562a5d4c90ef513ef83%2Ffordcity-07xx25-4.jpg 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/4f28f08/2147483647/strip/true/crop/3000x1684+0+187/resize/980x550!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Feb%2F8f%2F296777b64562a5d4c90ef513ef83%2Ffordcity-07xx25-4.jpg 2x" width="490" height="275" data-src="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/8241b29/2147483647/strip/true/crop/3000x1684+0+187/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Feb%2F8f%2F296777b64562a5d4c90ef513ef83%2Ffordcity-07xx25-4.jpg" data-lazy-load="true" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" > </picture> <div class="Figure-content"><figcaption class="Figure-caption"><p>Ford City Mall ubicada en 7601 S. Cicero Ave.</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Tyler Pasciak LaRiviere/Sun-Times file</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>Kurv tenía un contrato para comprar Ford City Mall a Namdar Realty Group en julio de 2025; los edificios cercanos, como el cine AMC Ford City 14, no estaban incluidos en el trato.</p><p>El promotor inmobiliario anunció planes para convertir el centro comercial del suroeste de la ciudad en un campus industrial, zonificado para almacenamiento o manufactura ligera. Kurv estimó que el desarrollo costaría $150 millones y necesitaría que el Concejo Municipal aprobara el cambio de zonificación del sitio del centro comercial, de comercial a industrial.</p><p>Los planes actuales elevan el costo del desarrollo a $200 millones, probablemente debido a la nueva plaza, la estación de autobuses y trabajos de infraestructura adicionales. Según los planes actualizados, la calle 76th se reconstruiría como vía pública.</p><p>Kurv no respondió a una solicitud de comentarios.</p><p>Los cuatro edificios variarían en tamaño, con los dos más grandes de más de 300,000 pies cuadrados. Los otros dos edificios tendrían aproximadamente 200,000 pies cuadrados y 100,000 pies cuadrados.</p><p>Un estudio de tráfico realizado para el sitio concluyó que habría "significativamente menos tráfico total" en un parque industrial en comparación con Ford City Mall.</p><p>La corte <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz/2026/05/18/ordenan-el-cierre-de-ford-city-mall-para-antes-del-22-de-junio" target="_blank" >ordenó su cierre el 22 de junio</a> el 22 de junio, tras una audiencia. Greg Janes, asesor jurídico adjunto de la Ciudad de Chicago, dijo durante la audiencia que todas las partes del caso acordaron el cierre del 22 de junio.</p><p>A Namdar Realty Group <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz/2026/04/20/ford-city-mall-esta-a-punto-de-cerrar-tras-falta-de-reparaciones" target="_blank" >se le había dado siete días</a> para presentar un plan para cerrar los comercios del centro comercial o desocupar el edificio, tras el cierre ordenado por la corte. La compañía no había realizado las reparaciones necesarias al deteriorado centro comercial; por ejemplo, un sistema de supresión de incendios defectuoso estaba provocando inundaciones constantes. También hubo preocupaciones por cables expuestos y posibles socavones.</p><p>El cierre forzado se produjo tras años de ventas a la baja. Al momento del cierre, el centro comercial tenía alrededor de dos docenas de comercios, incluyendo a su último inquilino ancla, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz/2026/04/24/jcpenney-retrocede-de-su-cierre-en-ford-city-pero-el-centro-comercial-sigue-en-peligro" target="_blank" >JCPenney</a>. Entre otras tiendas estaban Foot Locker, Sam’s Furniture y Victoria’s Secret, aunque muchos comerciantes ya se habían ido del centro comercial antes de la orden de la corte.</p><p><i>Traducido con una herramienta de inteligencia artificial (IA) y editado por los seres humanos de </i><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz" target="_blank" ><i>La Voz Chicago</i></a><br></p>

entries.title: White Sox salvage Crosstown season series split, return home with four-game lead in AL Central
entries.summary: <p>A laugher would have been nice.</p><p>Even just a stiff breeze behind Jake Rogers’ seventh inning fly out to the wall, or a bloop hit with the bases loaded in the ninth, could have saved relief ace Grant Taylor from working back-to-back days.</p><p>For a bedraggled pitching staff facing another week of games before their next off day, a 3-0 victory at Wrigley Field to salvage a season series split, wasn’t a perfect salve for every sore hitter, every tired arm in the White Sox clubhouse. But it was a welcome one.</p><p>“There's kind of a general level of tiredness that sets in everywhere at this time of year,” said Braden Montgomery, who protected a 1-0 lead with an outfield assist in the sixth, and lengthened it with a two-run double off the tip of first baseman Michael Busch’s glove in the eighth. “When you're in between the white lines, there's nothing else to pay attention to."</p><p>It also kind of fit how this White Sox team always manages to stay afloat.</p><p>Just when Tyrone Taylor’s leadoff double in front of NL MVP candidate Pete Crow-Armstrong in the sixth spelled trouble, Montgomery — their Maserati of a right field prospect who has yet to even reach third gear — <a class="Link" href="https://x.com/SlangsOnSports/status/2090167519562621016?s=20" target="_blank" ><u>uncorked a 95 mph bullet</u></a> to catch Taylor advancing to third. Just when it looked like Alex Bregman, Tuesday’s walk-off villain, was about to tie things up with a blast to left in the seventh, the converted infielder the Sox play out there, who used to play Division II ball downstate in a home stadium called “The Corn Crib,” scaled the Wrigley Field ivy for a leaping catch.</p><p>“It was kind of tricky with that basket,” said Sam Antonacci, who tried to ignore the brick wall into which he was jumping. “You want to put it out of your mind. If you have any doubt like that, odds are you're probably not going to come around with it.”</p><p>Just when it seemed like the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/08/18/white-sox-noah-schultz-hagen-smith-tanner-mcdougal-david-sandlin-brian-bannister-will-venable-erick-fedde-jose-urquidy-davis-martin-al-central" target="_blank" ><u>Sox were well and truly out of starting pitching</u></a>, Jose Urquidy found a level he hadn’t felt since losing most of the last two seasons to injury, since playoff runs with the Astros, to blank the Cubs — MLB’s second-best scoring offense — for six innings.</p><p>“Two or three years ago, 2023, that was my last game in the postseason,” Urquidy said of the last time he felt as good as he did Wednesday. I’ve been waiting for this kind of outing, trying to be dominant during the game. I’m very happy to have this feeling.”</p><p>With the win, the Sox are actually just 34-33 since June 1; a fact obscured by them leading an AL Central that has no other winning teams for almost all of that time. But that span also includes 35 games without All-Star slugger Munetaka Murakami, just one four-game losing streak at any point, and two grueling pockets of schedule; the latter of which only begins to level off after Thursday’s makeup game with the NL East-leading Braves.</p><p>“We don’t know any better, honestly,” said veteran Andrew Benintendi, who hit a sixth-inning RBI single off Clay Holmes, a starter the Sox scouted ahead of the trade deadline. “Regardless of what happens, each day we turn the page pretty quickly.”</p><p>Now a series-salvaging victory against their North Side neighbors, right after two exhausting walk-off losses, puts the Sox at a 33-32 run differential for the season against a Cubs team with the fifth-best record in MLB. Once more, when it looked like they shouldn’t be able to, they hung tough with a heavy hitter. And with a four-game AL Central lead, they return south, where they have the fourth-best home record in MLB.</p><p>“Really tough road trip with Detroit and then the Cubs,” said manager Will Venable. “You go 4-2 on that road trip, really every one of those games we're in, we played well. Of course we weren't perfect, but just so proud of the guys.”</p><div class="PageListL" data-module data-hide-authors="true" data-hide-categories="true" data-hide-dates="true" entries.title: Splitsville! Stellar Cubs-White Sox season series ends tied 3-3
entries.summary: <p>Splitsville.</p><p>Chicago baseball fans might not love it, but they won’t forget it.</p><p>With the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox" target="_blank" >White Sox</a> beating the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" target="_blank" >Cubs</a> 3-0 Wednesday at Wrigley Field, the best Crosstown season series of ’em all ended in a 3-3 deadlock. Yes, you read that correctly — the best, since interleague play began in the major leagues in 1997.</p><p>(No, I wasn’t around to see the “Hitless Wonders” Sox upset the Cubs in six games in the 1906 World Series. I’m sure it was a real doozy.)</p><p>“It’s kind of like a tie, I guess, in a sense,” said Sox rookie left fielder Sam Antonacci, his math skills in full effect. “Just six overall really good games, really good teams going at it.</p><p>“Feels like we need more games to decide the winner.”</p><p>Now that’s the spirit.</p><p>Coming into the season, the Crosstown rivalry had a nice list of stellar moments. The first walk-off homer, hit by the Cubs’ Brant Brown in 1998. The walk-off grand slam — the first of those in interleague play across the big leagues — belted by the Sox’ Carlos Lee in 2001. The Sox rallying from 8-0 down, supercharged by a pair of Paul Konerko dingers, to win in 2002. The long ball by the Cubs’ Aramis Ramirez for a walk-off in 2008, when both playoff-bound teams were in first place. The Sox’ Eloy Jimenez blasting off in the ninth against his former employers in 2019. Cubs walk-off homers by Christopher Morel in 2023 and Mike Tauchman in 2024.</p><p>But this season’s series on both sides of town delivered at such a high level, it seemed to light a fire under Chicago’s entire baseball fandom. That simply doesn’t happen very often, in large part because the Cubs and Sox are good at the same time approximately as often as a total solar eclipse is visible from your Barcalounger. But with the Sox in first place in the American League Central (yes, they’re in a terrible division) and the Cubs rolling toward the National League’s top wild-card spot (no, they’re not catching the Brewers), the spotlight was bright — and intoxicating chaos unfolded.</p><p>How do you top the way the Sox fought back in May after losing the first of three games at Rate Field? In Game 2 of that series, Munetaka Murakami loudly introduced himself to Cubs fans who’d been ignoring his exploits, launching a pair of homers. Three other Sox players — including the strikingly emergent Miguel Vargas — went deep in a blowout. Then, in the finale, the teams traded three-run shots in the ninth inning to force extra innings, setting the stage for unlikely hero Edgar Quero to win it for the Sox with a two-run homer in the 10th.</p><p>But Cubs superstar Pete Crow-Armstrong — three months after running his mouth at the Rate’s outfield fence and getting himself into trouble — kicked everything up a notch with his performance at Wrigley, where he led off Games 1 and 2 with homers and ended the first game in the 10th with a two-run blast. Teammate Alex Bregman added a walk-off base hit in the ninth a night later in a game that ended around midnight after a late-inning rain delay. Heavy drama.</p><p>To earn a season split — after going 2-12 against the Cubs from 2023 to 2025 — the Sox needed a hero in the finale. Enter Jose Urquidy, a name from World Series past who more recently had faded beyond obscurity. In 2024, the right-hander had Tommy John surgery. Less than four weeks ago, the Sox made a deal with the Pirates to get him, sending a reliever named Felix Doroteo in return. As a general rule, when you’re traded for what sounds more like a corn chip than a high-end prospect, the expectations of you tend to be low.</p><p>But Urquidy, days after being called up from Triple-A at 31, entered in the third inning and went six glorious shutout frames, looking for a couple of hours like the finest starter on either team’s roster.</p><p>You’ve got to be Urquidy-ing me. Who could’ve seen that coming?</p><p>“For sure, it’s been very hard,” he said, shaking his head, after the TV cameras had left his locker in the visiting clubhouse. “It took me two years to be at this point, to feel my body’s ready to be in the big leagues.”</p><p>But now?</p><p>“I’m feeling healthy,” he said. “I’m feeling the whole world. I’m very happy to have this feeling.”</p><p>It was some kind of season series. For many of the tough-minded, but inexperienced, Sox, it was a first-of-its-kind atmosphere.</p><p>“Up there, for sure,” center fielder Tristan Peters said. “Very electric. You’ve got people fighting in the stands. There’s boos. There’s cheers. Man — intense.”</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/19/white-sox-cubs-crosstown-series-jose-urquidy-tyrone-taylor-clay-holmes-braden-montgomery" >White Sox hold Cubs to two hits, avoid sweep with shutout win in Crosstown series finale</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/19/cubs-white-sox-crosstown-series-clay-holmes-pete-crow-armstrong-alex-bregman-daniel-palencia-gabriel-arias" >Cubs showed off playoff potential with Crosstown series win over postseason-caliber White Sox team</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/16/white-sox-cubs-crosstown-rivalry-wrigley-field-chicago" target="_blank" >White Sox at Cubs — the Crosstown Come-Up — takes the stage Monday, a series this city deserves</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p>

entries.title: Absuelven a un hombre que pateó a un novillo en la cabeza durante coleadero en los suburbios
entries.summary: <p>No parece haber mucho debate sobre si Socorro Barrientos, de 68 años, pateó repetidamente a un novillo en la cabeza el año pasado en un jaripeo realizado en los suburbios del noroeste, lo que llevó a que se le imputara un cargo por crueldad hacia los animales en su contra.</p><p>En cambio, al explicar un veredicto de no culpable dictado la semana pasada en el caso de Barrientos, el juez Justin Hansen, del Condado de McHenry, se centró en gran medida en cómo aterrizaron y se dieron las patadas, con un video de dron que muestra al novillo tendido justo fuera del corral, incapaz —o sin ganas— de ponerse de pie mientras un pie descendía sobre él diez o más veces.</p><p>Aunque dijo que “encontré esta decisión difícil”, —y señaló que el comportamiento de Barrientos “quizá no fue muy amable”— Hansen dijo, “No lo considero cruel” a través de su análisis.</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-8e0000" name="module-8e0000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h3>La Voz Chicago WhatsApp</h3>Encuentra más noticias en nuestro canal de WhatsApp. <a class="Link" href="https://www.whatsapp.com/channel/0029Vb0XT1XCHDylm3rCs40P" target="_blank" ><b>Síguenos.</b></a></div> </div><p>No pareció que la intención del acusado fuera “lesionar a la vaca o infligir dolor o sufrimiento”, dijo Hansen el jueves en una sala de la Corte en Woodstock. “Creo que intentó mover a la vaca de nuevo a la posición de pie”.</p><p>Hansen dijo que Barrientos no usó la “punta de su bota” para patear al animal y que “esta acción del acusado parece ser una con poca o ninguna ventaja”.</p><p>Si Barrientos hubiera estado “frente a la vaca y apoyado firmemente un pie y luego se hubiera echado hacia atrás” como si estuviera “pateando un balón”, eso habría sido “una maniobra muy diferente”, explicó Hansen.</p><p>“No hay indicios de que el animal esté afectado o molesto” por lo ocurrido, ya que “el video no muestra” que el animal “exprese ninguna reacción”.</p><p>Hansen también se refirió a una veterinaria que testificó que el novillo experimentó “daño, miedo y trauma” y sufrió patadas “bruscas”: “Creo que la doctora tiene buenas intenciones”, pero no la encontró “particularmente persuasiva”.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div para Animales trata el “trato cruel”, diciendo en parte: “Ninguna persona ni propietario podrá golpear, tratar cruelmente, atormentar, dejar morir de hambre, sobrecargar de trabajo ni abusar de otro modo de ningún animal”.</p><p>Pero Hansen dijo que “no existe una definición clara que establezca el umbral de lo que constituye el trato cruel a un animal”.</p><p>“‘Cruel’ no está definido en la ley”, añadió.</p><p>Nathan Noble, el abogado de Barrientos, dijo, “El juez tomó la decisión correcta. Es lamentable que esto siquiera se haya imputado en primer lugar”.</p><p>La fiscalía del Condado de McHenry, que procesó el caso, no respondió de inmediato las llamadas para hacer comentarios.</p><p>Jodie Wiederkehr, residente de Chicago y miembro del grupo por los derechos de los animales SHARK, describió el fallo como “trágico” y dijo que “patear a un animal en la cara href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz/2026/08/06/defensores-con-drones-denuncian-coleaderos-en-los-suburbios-de-illinois-por-maltrato-animal" target="_blank" >una semana después de que otros tres class="Figure-content"><figcaption class="Figure-caption"><p>La propiedad del Condado de McHenry donde se celebró el año pasado un jaripeo que dio lugar a cargos penales contra varios hombres, incluido Socorro Barrientos.</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Robert Herguth / Sun-Times</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>Conocida como coleadero, el evento consiste en hombres a caballo persiguiendo novillos que huyen, agarrando sus colas y enrollándolas alrededor de sus botas o piernas hasta que se caen. A veces la práctica provoca el “desollamiento”, con la cola desgarrada. Los animales pueden resultar heridos de otras maneras. En algunos casos sufren fracturas de patas.</p><p>Esos tres hombres se declararon culpables, pidieron disculpas y dijeron que no tenían la intención de lastimar a los novillos.</p><p>Una quinta persona, un menor de Lockport, fue inicialmente implicada, pero ese caso luego fue desestimado.</p><p>Todos los cargos se basaron al menos en parte en video de dron tomado en secreto por SHARK, siglas de Showing Animals Respect and Kindness, que ha criticado los rodeos de estilo mexicano y los rodeos tradicionales estadounidenses durante años.</p><p>La Ley de Cuidado Humano para Animales no sólo tipifica como delito el maltrato directo de mascotas y ganado, sino que también obliga a los propietarios de animales a proporcionar “atención veterinaria cuando sea necesaria para prevenir el sufrimiento”.</p><p>Algunos defensores de los animales han expresado su preocupación de que la ley es demasiado vaga para detener de forma consistente eventos de jaripeo como el coleadero, por lo que se ha propuesto legislación tanto en la Asamblea General de Illinois como en la Junta del Condado de McHenry para prohibir explícitamente la práctica.</p><p>Ninguna de las medidas se aprobó este año, pero se espera que ambos órganos legislativos vuelvan a discutir el tema, aunque en el Condado de McHenry, la miembro de la Junta, Pam Althoff, dijo que eso podría implicar restricciones a propuestas de zonificación.</p><p><i>Traducido con una herramienta de inteligencia artificial (IA) y editado por los seres humanos de </i><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz" target="_blank" ><i>La Voz Chicago</i></a></p>

entries.title: How are Cubs liking trade-deadline acquisitions Kevin Gausman, Clay Holmes? ‘They’re going to help us a lot’
entries.summary: <p>If you had to choose one word to sum up Clay Holmes’ 2026, what would it be?</p><p>“He’s been disgusting all season, man,” outfielder Tyrone Taylor said.</p><p>That’s a compliment, by the way.</p><p>Holmes has indeed been “disgusting” throughout his career, a former All-Star closer turned effective starter who was one of the big trade-deadline additions for a <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" >Cubs</a> team seeking postseason glory.</p><p>Taylor played with Holmes on the Mets the last two seasons, seeing the right-hander’s great 2025 and even better start to 2026 before a leg injury wiped out three months of his campaign.</p><p>But Holmes is healthy again and has pitched well in his second and third turns as a Cub, following up 6⅔ scoreless innings against the Cardinals last weekend with 5⅓ innings of one-run ball against the White Sox on Wednesday.</p><p>It’s been grounders aplenty from the sinkerballer, who’s looked worthy of <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/03/cubs-mlb-trade-deadline-jed-hoyer-top-prospects-trades-kevin-gausman-clay-holmes-ryan-zeferjahn-braxton-garrett-tyrone-taylor" >Jed Hoyer’s win-now statement</a>, the surrender of the Cubs’ No. 2 prospect, infielder Jefferson Rojas, to rent Holmes for a planned October run.</p><p>Certainly, the players around Holmes help; the Cubs own baseball’s best defense and the second highest scoring offense in the sport.</p><p>“More times than not, if you can keep this team in the game, then something special can happen,” Holmes said. “I have zero ounce or fear of getting the ball on the ground. I know that if I do that time and time again, a lot of good things are going to happen behind me, even with guys on.</p><p>“Sometimes it’s easy to feel like you have to shy away from it with runners on … but even with runners on, there’s a lot of confidence. I can trust the contact that I get and that outs are going to be made. … It frees you up, and it allows you to pitch with a lot of confidence.”</p><p>It’s been three starts apiece now in Cubs uniforms for Holmes and fellow trade-deadline addition Kevin Gausman, two righties who Hoyer slotted in at the top of the team’s starting rotation to bolster a pitching staff that had its depth tested throughout the summer.</p><p>“They’re super pro,” second baseman Nico Hoerner said. “They’re guys that have had success in a lot of different places. It’s been great to have them.</p><p>“They’re going to help us a lot.”</p><p>That’s not to say it’s all been sunshine and rainbows and fans can start lining up for a parade.</p><p>Holmes looked understandably rusty in his debut, allowing four runs in four innings, though he’s bounced back nicely. Gausman, meanwhile, has had a couple tough nights after a terrific first outing, when he threw seven innings of two-run ball against the Royals.</p><p>The right-hander was tagged for six runs against the Nationals’ best-in-baseball offense last week, then <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/18/cubs-kevin-gausman-injury-hand-thumb-crosstown-white-sox-trade-deadline-rotation" >left Tuesday’s start early with a hand cramp</a>, not making it out of the fifth inning in either outing.</p><p>“It’s pretty frustrating, to be honest, my first start [at Wrigley Field] as a Cub, obviously not what I’m trying to do,” Gausman said after Tuesday’s game. “It’s only the second time, I think, in my career that I left the game [with an injury].</p><p>“I’ve had [the cramping] happen, but usually it’s when I’m over 100 pitches, that’s when I run into it. I’ve never had it happen that early in an outing. That’s why it’s kind of frustrating.”</p><p>But these guys’ track records are still speaking for themselves inside the Cubs’ clubhouse. Gausman pitched well in helping the Blue Jays to the doorstep of a World Series win last fall, while Holmes pitched for the Yankees in all five games of the previous year’s Fall Classic.</p><p>Both guys lost to the Dodgers, something they’d surely be happy to avenge.</p><p>The Cubs have had their sights on winning the season’s final game — something that will require toppling the Dodgers, not to mention the first-place, division-rival Brewers — from the jump this year, and Hoyer’s import of both Gausman and Holmes have a lot to do with how the team plans to do it.</p><p>The reviews so far?</p><p>“Disgusting.”</p><p></p><bsp-listcarousel class="PageListE" data-module data-column-count=3 data-hide-authors="true" data-hide-categories="true" data-hide-dates="true" Devon Hayakawa directs. From Aug. 26-Oct. 11 at Paramount Theatre, 23 E. Galena Blvd., Aurora. Tickets: $34-$109. Visit <a class="Link" href="http://paramountaurora.com" target="_blank" ><u>paramountaurora.com</u></a>.</li><li>Irene Sankoff and David Hein’s musical<b> “Come From Away”</b> tells the true story of the tiny town of Gander, Newfoundland, whose residents took in 7,000 strangers when air space was closed on Sept. 11, 2001. Jessica Fisch directs. From Aug. 26-Oct. 18 at Marriott Theatre, 10 Marriott Dr., Lincolnshire. Tickets: $78+. Visit <a class="Link" href="http://marriotttheatre.com" target="_blank" ><u>marriotttheatre.com</u></a>.</li><li>Mark Pracht’s <b>“Shane”</b> is a world premiere adaptation of Jack Schaefer’s classic Western novel about a mysterious stranger who takes a job as a farm hand in the Wyoming Territory in 1889. Pracht directs. From Aug. 21-Oct. 4 at City Lit Theater, 1020 W. Bryn Mawr Ave. Tickets: $40. Visit <a class="Link" href="http://citylit.org" target="_blank" ><u>citylit.org</u></a>.</li></ul><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-250000" name="image-250000"></a> <picture data-crop="medium"> <source type="image/webp" width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/f105495/2147483647/strip/true/crop/1800x1010+0+95/resize/490x275!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fde%2Fc2%2F892c86b142b585e6a583903abd99%2Fjoan-crawford-goes-to-hell-photo-by-rick-aguilar-studios.jpg 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/8088749/2147483647/strip/true/crop/1800x1010+0+95/resize/980x550!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fde%2Fc2%2F892c86b142b585e6a583903abd99%2Fjoan-crawford-goes-to-hell-photo-by-rick-aguilar-studios.jpg 2x" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <source width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/7123d49/2147483647/strip/true/crop/1800x1010+0+95/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fde%2Fc2%2F892c86b142b585e6a583903abd99%2Fjoan-crawford-goes-to-hell-photo-by-rick-aguilar-studios.jpg" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <img class="Image" alt="Joan Crawford Goes To Hell - entries.title: Cubs showed off playoff potential with Crosstown series win over postseason-caliber White Sox team
entries.summary: <p>The overwhelming majority of the guys to play for the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" >Cubs</a> aren’t Chicago born and bred, so excuse them for not seeing the Crosstown series against the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox" >White Sox</a> as the biggest three days of the year.</p><p>But for at least the first two nights of this week’s series, they played like it had been circled on their calendars, grabbing a pair of walk-off wins against a first-place team in what could easily be described as a playoff-type atmosphere at Wrigley Field.</p><p>The Cubs did next to nothing offensively in Wednesday’s series finale, a 3-0 loss in which they only mustered two hits. But it was another series win against a postseason-caliber team.</p><p>If the back half of August and the whole of September are about readying for the challenges of playoff baseball, they made more than a couple statements about what they’re capable of this week.</p><p>“You can feel the attention to detail, the energy this group plays with,” righty starter <b>Clay Holmes</b> said. “You can feel there’s a strong desire to be really good.</p><p>“We know what we’re capable of, and you see people go about their work and how they show up for gametime with that in mind. When you have 26 guys that are doing that, showing up every day with that desire … good things are going to happen.”</p><p>Forget <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/17/cubs-white-sox-crosstown-series-playoffs-standings-nl-central-al-central-pete-crow-armstrong-seiya-suzuki" >the Cubs-Sox championship rematch talk</a> for now. This team is doing it’s whole “one game at a time” thing.</p><p>But in one game at a time, they got <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/17/pete-crow-armstrongs-walk-off-homer-gives-cubs-win-over-white-sox-in-back-and-forth-crosstown-clash" >an MVP display from center fielder <b>Pete Crow-Armstrong</b></a> and another marquee moment in third baseman <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/18/cubs-white-sox-crosstown-alex-bregman-pete-crow-armstrong-munetaka-murakami-kevin-gausman" ><b>Alex Bregman</b>’s late-summer awakening</a>, previewing a couple potential superstars of October.</p><p>The Cubs didn’t need the Sox to come up Lake Shore Drive to affirm they’re able to make some noise in the postseason. Just two weeks back, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/05/cubs-pete-crow-armstrong-shohei-ohtani-nl-mvp-race-dodgers-playoffs-craig-counsell-shota-imanaga" >they swept the Dodgers in this ballpark</a>. They’ve won twice as many games as they’ve lost (40-20) since June 11 and own the fifth best record in baseball.</p><p>After a streaky start to the campaign — two 10-game win streaks early, then a 10-game losing streak — things have stabilized, and they look like contenders.</p><p>“We’ve had stretches this year earlier in the year where we’ve been the hottest team in baseball, then the coldest team in baseball, then the hottest team in baseball again,” Bregman said. “The main thing in this second half is just being consistent and playing consistent baseball, and I feel like we’ve done a good job of that in all three phases of the game.”</p><h3><b>Enter Arias</b></h3><h3></h3><p>With shortstop <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/18/dansby-swansons-presence-will-be-part-of-cubs-efforts-to-weather-his-absence-he-turns-into-another-coach" ><b>Dansby Swanson</b> on the IL</a> and expected to miss four weeks, the Cubs added to their infield mix Wednesday, claiming veteran infielder <b>Gabriel Arias</b> off waivers.</p><p>Arias, a veteran of five major league seasons, played in 44 games with the Guardians and Mets this year, batting .235 with a career-best .645 OPS and appearances at all four infield positions.</p><h3><b>Palencia back Friday</b></h3><h3></h3><p>Righty reliever <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/18/cubs-bullpen-playoffs-daniel-palencia-injury-jacob-webb-closer-ryan-zeferjahn-david-peterson-craig-counsell-pete-crow-armstrong-seiya-suzuki" ><b>Daniel Palencia</b> will return</a> from the injured list Friday.</p><p>Palencia has been on the IL for more than two months working back from elbow inflammation, limited to only 16⅔ major league innings this season.</p><h3><b>Back into the rotation</b></h3><h3></h3><p>Righty pitcher <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/17/cubs-injuries-dansby-swanson-oblique-edward-cabrera-blister-nico-hoerner-pedro-ramizrez-craig-counsell-david-peterson-javier-assad-rotation-bullpen" ><b>Edward Cabrera’s</b> trip to the IL</a> with a blister created a vacancy in the Cubs’ rotation, which will be filled by the guy he bumped to the bullpen last weekend.</p><p>Lefty <b>David Peterson</b> will step back in to a starting role after a short turn as a reliever that was forced by Cabrera's brief return from a hamstring injury.</p><p>Peterson will start Saturday night against the Mariners in Seattle.</p><p></p><bsp-listcarousel class="PageListE" data-module data-column-count=3 data-hide-authors="true" data-hide-categories="true" data-hide-dates="true" entries.title: Welch skips Illinois State Fair, where Democrats focus on Trump instead of harassment scandal
entries.summary: <p>SPRINGFIELD — Ethics concerns in the Illinois House took a back seat to bashing President Donald Trump Wednesday for Democrats at the Illinois State Fair, where the supermajority party launched its sprint to November’s general election with familiar critiques of Republicans — and without embattled Speaker Emanuel “Chris” Welch in attendance.</p><p>Welch sat out Governor’s Day festivities in the capital after Springfield’s latest sexual harassment scandal, which has <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/springfield/2026/08/05/welch-benton-harassment-working-group-cassidy" target="_blank" ><u>raised questions about the speaker’s handling of misconduct allegations</u></a> against disgraced former state Rep. Harry Benton, who resigned last month in the face of complaints from three women.</p><p>The speaker typically holds court with the media alongside the state’s other top Democratic power players at the fair, where the late summer scents of fried food and farm animals signal the home stretch of campaign season.</p><p>But after attending a series of Springfield fundraisers Tuesday night, Welch headed home for his daughter’s first day of school, according to a spokesperson.</p><p>That left members of his caucus to field questions about whether Welch should have directed $1.4 million to Benton’s 2024 reelection campaign, when the speaker knew of a complaint well before the one that led to the Plainfield Democrat’s ouster.</p><p>“I think that it has played out, and he did what he can,” Illinois Democratic Party Chair Lisa Hernandez told the Sun-Times. “I just see that he's still doing all he can to put processes in place so this never happens.”</p><p>Hernandez, the influential Cicero representative who serves as deputy majority leader of Welch’s super-majority caucus, called it “a lesson learned, that you must continue, no matter what, every year … looking at your policies in place — that whether you refine them, or do a little extra, we must always be on top of it. So I think the work is being done.”</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item"> <bsp-carousel class="Carousel Enhancement" data-align-center> <a class="AnchorLink" aria-label="Next"> <svg class="FlickityCustomNavigation-button-icon"><use xlink:href="#icon-right"></use></svg> </button> </div> </div></div> </bsp-carousel> </div> </div><p>During an apology tour with select media outlets earlier this month, Welch said he regretted supporting Benton’s reelection but maintained he was hamstrung because the victim did not want to file a formal complaint.</p><p>Welch — who also apologized for sending heart-eye emojis in social media messages to a complainant and inviting her to a bar via an encrypted messaging app — announced a new House working group tasked with developing remedies for Springfield’s persistent culture of sexual harassment.</p><p>Three members initially slated to serve on the group have turned it down, including Chicago state Rep. Kelly Cassidy, who dismissed it as paying “lip service” to a serious issue.</p><p>Hernandez said she’s “very confident that they're going to have something in place that we're all going to be comfortable with. But [that’s] not to say that we don't keep on doing better." </p><p>Gov. JB Pritzker urged the group to work quickly.</p><p>“There are models for sexual harassment policies across the nation, in legislatures, in large corporations, in nonprofit organizations,” Pritzker said after a fairgrounds rally. “It seems like it would be relatively easy to look at a few of those models, have a few people get together around that, and make a decision about which one works best for the state of Illinois.</p><p>“We've got to make sure people know what the reporting mechanisms are and that it is dealt with in a timely fashion. I don't think those things were happening under the system that the House of Representatives had before, and I know the speaker has admitted that and now is looking for a solution.” </p><p>Republicans, who get their day at the fair Thursday, tried to make hay of the scandal with placards posted around the grounds declaring that Welch “covered up sexual harassment,” and, nodding at his emojis, that he’s “been spreading the love.”</p><h3></h3><h3><b>Trump jabs and mayoral jockeying</b></h3><p>Democrats, meanwhile, kept the focus on “everything we do to fight for families that Trump has too often tossed aside,” as a fiery U.S. Sen. Tammy Duckworth told more than 2,000 attendees at the annual Illinois Democratic County Chairs’ Association Brunch.</p><p>“I cannot wait to get back into the majority because I am f- - - - - - tired of fixing things that he broke,” Duckworth said to raucous applause.</p><p>Democrats also feted retiring U.S. Sen. Dick Durbin, who said he’s “tried to return the favor, to make sure I look back on that ladder and help somebody up behind me. That is the future of our party, and we’ve got to remember it at every possible level.” </p><p>Chicago mayoral politics made their way downstate, too, as outgoing state comptroller and fifth-floor <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/news/2026/06/03/susana-mendoza-announces-campaign-for-chicago-mayor" target="_blank" ><u>City Hall hopeful Susana Mendoza</u></a> told brunch attendees that “you deserve a candidate who's going to be all-in for the position that they're asking you to support them for, the statewide position.”</p><p>That was a not-so-subtle jab at Alexi Giannoulias, who’s running for a second term at the state level while mounting <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/08/02/alexi-giannoulias-chicago-mayor-candidate-2027-february-election-secretary-of-state" target="_blank" ><u>his own campaign for mayor</u></a>.</p><p>Giannoulias shrugged it off while rubbing shoulders at the fair.</p><p>“No one's talking about that. I'm proud of the work that we've done in the secretary of state's office. It is awkward coming from her,” he said. “You don't quit the job you're in while you're interviewing for the next one.”</p>

entries.title: 3 men shot in Humboldt Park parking lot
entries.summary: <p>Three men were shot in Humboldt Park Wednesday afternoon, according to Chicago police.</p><p>The three men — ages 22, 25 and 33 — were in a parking lot in the 4000 block of West Hirsch Street around noon when a vehicle pulled up and a passenger fired shots at them, police said. </p><p>The 25-year-old was shot in his right armpit and taken to Stroger Hospital in critical condition.</p><p>The 22-year-old transported himself to Norwegian Hospital after being shot in his abdomen, and was listed in critical condition, police said. The 33-year-old also brought himself to the same hospital to be treated for a gunshot wound to his right hand. He was listed in good condition.</p><p>No one is in custody.<br></p>

entries.title: The Bears are plagued with injuries — but WR Rome Odunze's foot feels great
entries.summary: <p>During a preseason that seems to claim a new <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> player to injury almost each practice day, Rome Odunze stands tall for one reason — he hasn’t gone down.</p><p>The receiver who declared during the Bears’ offseason program that his once-injured foot had become a <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/07/30/bears-wr-rome-odunze-backtracks-on-new-normal-comment-says-foot-is-completely-fine" target="_blank" >“new normal”</a> has played every relevant down in practice. He feels, and looks, healthy. He’s fast down the field and quick with his cuts. He runs decisively.</p><p>“I don't feel it . . .” he said. “I don't really think about it.”</p><p>His coaches do, and remember to watch Odunze’s gait. This far it looks the same as it did early last season, before a series of foot injuries held him out for five regular-season games and limited in even more.</p><p>“I'm always looking, but I haven't seen anything — anything,” receivers coach Antwaan Randle El said Wednesday. “He's been running smooth, getting out of his routes, and doing everything we’ve asked him to do.”</p><p>Odunze and the Bears’ training staff developed a routine that has kept his right foot, in which he suffered a stress fracture last year, feeling good. The only pain he has felt is soreness from running around in cleats for hours at a time, and that’s common for most players.</p><p>The proof of his return to health has shown up in the speed board that shows players who ran the fastest in that day’s practice. Odunze is regularly near the top.</p><p>Now he needs to do what the Bears drafted him in the first round to do — be the team’s No. 1 receiver. They can decide as soon as January whether to pick up his fifth-year option — or let him leave after 2027. For all the buzz about Luther Burden entering camp — coach Ben Johnson said he’d buy stock in the second-year former second-round pick — Odunze is the prototypical lead receiver. He’s 6-3, 214 pounds with tremendous jumping ability.</p><p>The Bears picked Odunze for his ability to use his size to make contested catches, whether deep shots or red-zone jump balls.</p><p>“The 1-on-1, 50-50 ball is one of my expertises,” Odunze said.</p><p>Johnson is notorious for saying he doesn’t want to throw 50-50 balls; he wants to draw up plays that make them more like a 90-10. But the team has put in more deep shots this year than they had in the playbook last year, offensive coordinator Press Taylor said.</p><p>That’s because of Odunze.</p><p>“You see the explosion in his game,” Taylor said. “You see the contested catch ability that he has. . . . We've made it a point of emphasis to try to push the ball down the field on some contested go balls because that's obviously a strength of his. That's something we didn't feature much as a coaching staff last year.”</p><p>Inside the red zone, a duo of Odunze and tight end Colston Loveland will make defenses choose between whom they want to double-team — and who they want to leave in man coverage for a jump ball. In seven-on-seven drills Wednesday, Odunze caught two touchdowns from quarterback Caleb Williams in red-zone situations.</p><p>The Bears’ strength is their roster of skill-position players on offense. Without Odunze, though, the wide receiver room gets shallow fast. Burden is rehabbing a groin injury but is expected to back for the start of the season and Kalif Raymond is a veteran with speed. Jahdae Walker has half a season’s worth of experience and Zavion Thomas is a rookie.</p><p>Entering his third season, Odunze should be treated like a veteran.</p><p>“I think you're seeing a little bit even more detail in his routes show up as we've gone — that's to be expected,” Taylor said. “It's Year 3. He's heard all the coaching points on this. He understands where he's supposed to be when he's supposed to be there.”</p><p>The same can be said of two receivers who will line up on the opposite sideline from Odunze in Thursday’s joint practice. The Washington alum considers the Bengals' Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins to be among the best wide receivers in the sport.</p><p>Odunze plans to steal a few glimpses at what the two do best.</p><p>“Tee just moves so well for his height,” Odunze said. “He's fluid in and out of his routes, and then he, you know, he has tremendous catch-point radius, going up contested catch. I feel like Ja’Marr is just like incredible after the catch as well, some of the catches that he makes over the middle as well as his go-ball chemistry with [quarterback] Joe [Burrow] — [that’s] something I'm looking to get and display with Caleb as well.”</p><p>So far, he looks the part, which is a relief.</p><p>“It’s good to see,” Randle El said.</p><bsp-list-loadmore class="PageListH"
